purpose: Post go-live settling framework for GPs — continuity and reliability over volume. Extends human-reviewed onboarding after Stage 7 Go-live.
boundaries: No guaranteed patient list size, earnings, or session growth
Session expansion only with rooms, nursing cover, and mutual reliability
Medicare provider numbers issued by Services Australia — not WMC
Metrics inform support — they are not recruitment KPIs

phases.label: Day 1
phases.outcome: Orientation complete; first patients with named support

phases.label: Week 1
phases.outcome: Daily systems and nursing handoffs become familiar

phases.label: Month 1
phases.outcome: Reliable sessions; early continuity; systems fluent

phases.label: Month 2
phases.outcome: List thickening; community literacy; predictable nursing partnership

phases.label: Month 3
phases.outcome: 90-day review; hold or staged expansion if capacity allows

day1: Complete orientation: emergency, privacy, rooms, treatment room, reception flow
Meet named nurse and reception lead; agree mid-list help cue
Consult only within the agreed session footprint
Invite continuity: offer to be the patient’s regular GP where appropriate
week1: Prioritise documentation quality; learn inbox/results conventions
Use nursing for appropriate treatment-room and preventive steps daily
Book clinically needed follow-ups to your own sessions when capacity allows
Learn local referral preferences and after-hours/escalation paths
Do not request extra sessions — reliability first
month1: Establish a predictable weekly rhythm patients and reception can trust
Complete one recall/results hygiene review with practice support
Agree booking-length notes with reception for longer presentations
Keep continuity language consistent with returning patients
Log systems friction once in writing so it can be owned
month2: Deepen nursing partnership on care plans, immunisation, credentialed procedures
Grow known-patient share ethically — no gaming allocations
Apply catchment literacy (mental health, women’s health, skin, emerging CDM) inside GP care
Optional: introductions to key local shared-care contacts via the practice
Raise unmet demand as a capacity conversation, not a volume demand
month3: Prepare for structured 90-day review (clinical, systems, sessions, wellbeing)
Decide with the practice: hold footprint, adjust days, or staged expansion if rooms and nursing allow
Confirm clinical interest pathways that fit credentialing and team capacity
Write down personal operating norms that work here
Measure success as sustainable continuity — not a patient-count target

day1: Roster named clinical and admin buddy; complete orientation sign-off
Match HotDoc/roster visibility to agreed sessions only
Brief nursing on new GP preferences and escalation
Give reception a continuity offer script — no overselling
Protect first lists from overbooking or overflow dumping
Hold end-of-day debrief and log blockers
week1: Soft check-in Day 2–5 (5–10 min); log issues on the settling case
Nursing: proactively offer treatment-room capacity on consulting days
Introduce peer GPs on overlapping days
Do not expand published sessions without mutual written agreement
month1: Audit follow-ups landing on the correct GP; confirm recalls enabled
Close or assign owners for Week 1 friction items
Optional: share de-identified book mix vs catchment expectations
month2: Support ethical list-building (return bookings, accurate HotDoc/team profile)
Verify procedural credentials before any public interest promotion
Offer hospital shared-care orientation if relevant
Record unmet demand by daypart for planning only
month3: Formal 90-day review with written summary for both parties
Expansion decision uses rooms + nursing cover + reliability criteria
Close settling status to BAU or a staged growth plan
No earnings or volume guarantees in review notes

checklist.item: Systems login and core templates verified
Named nurse and reception contacts confirmed
First session completed within agreed footprint
Daily nursing handoff used when clinically appropriate
Follow-ups booked to own sessions where capacity allows
Local referral and after-hours path known
Peer GP introduction on an overlapping day
Week 1 friction items closed or owned
Care-plan/preventive nursing partnership in routine use
Catchment case-mix literacy applied to interests
Formal 90-day review meeting and written summary
Expansion only if rooms + nursing + reliability met
Settling status closed to BAU or staged plan

metrics.label: Sessions delivered vs agreed
metrics.guidance: ≥95% of agreed sessions staffed as planned (excluding leave)

metrics.label: Return-patient booking rate
metrics.guidance: Upward trend M1→M3; no target gaming

metrics.label: Nursing-supported encounters
metrics.guidance: Stable non-zero use on consulting days

metrics.label: Results / inbox lag
metrics.guidance: Within practice standard by end of Month 1

metrics.label: Friction log open items
metrics.guidance: None open >14 days without owner by Month 1

metrics.label: Unmet demand by daypart
metrics.guidance: Inform Month 3 conversation only — not a maximise KPI

metrics.label: Doctor wellbeing pulse
metrics.guidance: No red without documented support action
